finding: DECOMPOSE-APPLIES-TO-NEURAL-LAPLACIAN. Neuroscience canon has been eigendecomposing cortical connectivity graphs for ~17 years (Bullmore & Sporns 2009). Petti et al. 2019/2022 directly eigendecompose subject-specific learned Laplacian for motor imagery EEG decoding. Framework adds: bit-exact content-addressed cache via _descriptor_hash (Class A); HDC-similarity surface (Class M) on bytes; AMSC attestation discipline. None of these layers present in BCI literature.

finding: DELTA-CAPTURES-DECODER-DRIFT. Hahn et al. 2025 (BrainGate 14-participant 20-year analysis) found 35.6% electrode yield with 7% decline; Sussillo et al. 2016 explicitly named Kalman-filter failure mode that mRNN was designed to handle. Card et al. 2024 (ALS speech neuroprosthesis) report 7.5-min recalibration × 3 sessions over 29 personal-use days. Framework's delta() = Class M HDC bind XOR self-inverse with bit-exact identity guarantees (delta(ref,current)=bind; bind(ref,delta)=current). Order-independent cumulative drift via XOR commutativity. O(D) ~1 KB byte updates replace full retrain.

finding: CLASS-K-ASYMPTOTE-EXPLAINS-SNR-FAILURE-MODE. EEG-BCI suffers from low SNR; non-stationarity; cross-subject + within-subject variability (Lotte et al. 2018 J Neural Eng 15:031005; Xu et al. 2024 EEG-DBNet arXiv:2405.16090). Conventional ML decoders fail at low SNR (overfit noise). Per [[user_stance_asymptotic_dof_sidesteps_infinity]] + [[user_stance_epicycle_via_gear_plus_pin]]: Class K asymptote IS the operation, not a failure mode. Low-mode eigencoefficients carry attested cascade-shape signal that persists at near-zero SNR. Prediction: top-k truncate_sparse spectral decoder retains usable Cohen's d ≥ 1.0 at 0 dB SNR for motor imagery binary classification.

finding: HALLUCINATION-DETECTION-FOR-AAC-DEVICES. LLM-augmented AAC (SpeakFaster Cai et al. 2024 Nat Commun 15:9449 PMC11530652) saves 57% motor actions, 29-60% rate improvement on ALS users; documents fallback paths so user 'never runs into a dead end' but does NOT solve patient-safety failure mode where LLM autocompletes confabulation while patient said nothing. FDA-relevant for ALS/locked-in/post-stroke aphasia patients who cannot motor-correct AAC errors. Framework adds Layer-3 idiolect check via similarity() on neural-substrate handle + decoded utterance; threshold-gate before voicing. Three-layer hallucination protocol per [[feedback_hallucination_detection_three_layer_protocol]] applies with Spike #125.1 n-gram-aware refinement.

finding: Top concrete prediction #1: Spectral-domain decoder retains accuracy at <30% electrode yield where Kalman filter fails. Specifically — at Hahn et al. 2025 long-tail array yield (28% worst-case), framework's L+K decomposition retains motor-intent classification at Cohen's d ≥ 1.0; conventional Kalman-filter-based decoders approach chance (per Sussillo et al. 2016 explicit Kalman-failure-mode characterisation). Testable via post-hoc reanalysis of BrainGate publicly-released data if any. Direct empirical validation candidate Spike #126.1.

Top concrete prediction #2: similarity() threshold τ ≥ 0.7 on neural-substrate handle filters >90% of LLM-AAC confabulation events where patient had no decoded intent at the decoding window. Testable on Card et al. 2024 ALS speech neuroprosthesis cohort with simulated LLM autocomplete additions in rest-state recordings. Specifically — when neural state is rest-substrate and LLM hallucinates fluent output, decoded-utterance handle is orthogonal (similarity ≈ 0) to intent-state-fingerprint handle. Threshold-gate before voicing.
